publishedExpectations.claim: Jump builds proprietary network infrastructure and three large purpose-built research data centers plus 100+ co-located compute environments near global exchanges.
Jump's stack includes custom ASIC/FPGA development for low-latency workloads and high-performance software frameworks written in C++, Python, Go, and Rust.
Jump's CTO: 'We build our own hardware, run large-scale AI workloads, and move faster than most tech companies. You can design something on Monday and see it in production by Friday.'
Engineers get ownership from day one — design, test and deploy in production — and the culture is described as autonomy, speed and trust with visibility across the entire technical stack.
Jump's careers page organises hiring around AI/ML, Technology, Trading and Signals groups, with dedicated campus recruiting contacts for students and new grads.

notes: Jump's site is employer-branding rather than process documentation: it confirms the stack (C++/Python/Go/Rust, FPGA/ASIC, co-located compute, proprietary networks) and the speed-and-ownership culture, but publishes no interview format. Community-reported patterns (unverified): algorithmically intense coding rounds, systems/low-latency design discussions, and a research-database puzzle screen for some teams. Candidates should treat specifics like interview counts, timelines or test names as unconfirmed. The reliable signal is that deep C++/systems depth and production ownership are what the firm advertises it needs.
